title: Creating Certificate Signing Requests for (Web Server) Certificates

blocks.text: To enable Browser Access for an application, you must upload its web server certificate. The certificate can be signed by a public certificate authority (CA) or be a self-signed certificate whose trust is established by your organization's public key infrastructure (PKI).
To create a certificate signing request (CSR) for a (web server) certificate:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Browser > Clientless Portal > Certificates.
Name: Enter a name for the CSR. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).

The common name does not need to be a wildcard domain.
Subject Alternate Name: Enter the Subject Alternate Name (SAN) for the CSR. Specifying a SAN allows the certificate to cover multiple hostnames (domains only). Click Add to add multiple SANs.
Click Create to generate content for the CSR.
The Certificates page automatically updates to display your pending CSR in the table, where you must upload the web server certificate.
